decisions.context: The service must return a fraud score within tens of milliseconds. Main requirements, in priority order: low scoring latency; continued operation during peak load; auditability of the model version and features used.

alternatives.label: Local service/API based model serving
cons: Peak-load availability: scales with host capacity

decisions.rationale: Peak-load availability decides in favor of independently scalable serving; it adds a network hop, so the service must be capacity-tested against the latency target.
consequences: Requires network calls on the authorization path.

decisions.decision: Persist and provide access to features
decisions.context: Auditors need to know which features produced each score, and the serving path has a tight latency budget. The design space identifies a feature store and general-purpose data stores as alternatives (d:4).

alternatives.label: Feature store
cons: Scoring latency: extra storage service may add a lookup

alternatives.label: Store features in data stores without specific support
pros: Scoring latency: can use an existing serving store
cons: Audit traceability: feature lineage needs separate handling

decisions.rationale: Audit traceability decides in favor of a feature store; its added serving lookup must fit within the latency budget.
consequences: Record the feature values or immutable references used for each score.
Feature lookup latency becomes part of the scoring path.

decisions.context: Each score must be attributable to a model version, while keeping the scoring service available through peaks. The design space lists concurrent versions, rollback, and a single production model (d:10).

alternatives.label: N versions in production
pros: Audit traceability: version is explicit per score
cons: Peak-load availability: concurrent versions consume capacity

alternatives.label: Rollback to previous model version
pros: Peak-load availability: provides a recovery path
cons: Audit traceability: rollback alone does not capture the version used per score

alternatives.label: Single model in production
cons: Audit traceability: requires separate version records

decisions.rationale: Audit traceability decides in favor of keeping versions identifiable in production; the cost is additional serving capacity for concurrent versions.
consequences: Tag every score with the model version used.
Capacity planning must account for concurrently deployed models.

decisions.decision: Track inputs and outputs in production
decisions.context: Auditors must be able to reconstruct which model version and features produced a score. The design space distinguishes model tracking from logging data and predictions (d:22).

alternatives.label: Model in-production tracking
pros: Audit traceability: tracks usage, inputs, and outputs
cons: Scoring latency: synchronous tracking may add overhead

alternatives.label: Monitoring or logging data and predictions
pros: Scoring latency: logging can be decoupled from scoring
cons: Audit traceability: logs may omit model-specific details

decisions.rationale: Audit traceability decides in favor of tracking model usage, inputs, and outputs; synchronous tracking overhead must be controlled to protect latency.
consequences: Persist model version and feature references with each score.
Tracking storage and retention add operational cost.

decisions.decision: Version the data used for model development
decisions.context: The audit requirement names production features, while reproducibility of model training data is not specified. Data versioning is available as a related design choice (d:11).

alternatives.label: Data versioning in code repository
pros: Audit traceability: keeps data references with code
cons: Audit traceability: large data may complicate repository use

decisions.rationale: Audit traceability favors explicitly versioned data; the brief does not require training-data reproducibility, so this choice supports broader model lineage at added repository cost.
consequences: Training runs must reference data versions.
The brief’s per-score audit record still needs production feature values or immutable references.

decisions.context: The scoring path has a tens-of-milliseconds target and must continue during peaks. The design space includes prediction-service performance testing (d:26).

alternatives.label: Prediction service performance testing
cons: Peak-load availability: representative peak traffic must be modeled

alternatives.label: System integration testing
cons: Latency: may not establish a response-time bound

alternatives.label: No testing
cons: Latency: no evidence of response time

decisions.rationale: The latency target decides in favor of performance testing; it costs representative test capacity and still needs realistic peak traffic to assess availability.
consequences: Measure latency under expected and peak load.
Test results depend on representative traffic and environment.

uncovered: Exact latency objective and percentile, transaction volume, and peak-load profile.
Availability target, failure behavior, and authorization fallback when scoring is unavailable.
Audit retention period, required explanation format, and whether feature values or immutable references are sufficient.
Model training, approval, and deployment controls; the design-space points checked had no attesting sources and are novel combinations.
